saskia l. van de gevel|virginia tech.summary: Van de Gevel started July 1, 2025 as dean of Virginia Tech's College of Natural Resources and Environment, succeeding Paul Winistorfer, who retired after 16 years -- so she follows an unusually long-tenured predecessor and is the first new leadership CNRE has seen in a generation. Her title is Dean only -- no experiment-station directorship -- but the college carries meaningful engagement infrastructure, including an associate dean for Extension, outreach and engagement, the Center for Leadership in Global Sustainability, and the Virginia Water Resources Research Center, over four units (fish and wildlife conservation, forest resources and environmental conservation, geography, sustainable biomaterials). She has a notably interdisciplinary profile -- forest science undergrad, forestry master's, geography doctorate -- brings a global perspective from living in both the Netherlands and the U.S., served as the National Geographic Society's geography steward for North Carolina and coordinator of the North Carolina Geographic Alliance, and won the 2023 Outstanding Service Award from the Southeastern Division of the American Association of Geographers.
